title: Plugin Anatomy — the directory and the manifest

questions.prompt: Your plugin ships three commands in `commands/` and its manifest also has `"commands": "./extra/status.md"`. After `/reload-plugins`, `/status` no longer exists but `claude plugin list` still shows the plugin as loaded with no error. Why?
options: The manifest path must start with `./`, so `./extra/status.md` was rejected and the folder silently kept the old commands
Setting the `commands` key replaces the default `commands/` scan instead of adding to it, so those three files are no longer read
Commands only load once a marketplace entry names them, which this plugin lacks
The files moved but the plugin kept a stale cache; `/reload-plugins` must be run twice for component folders to re-scan
questions.explanation: `commands`, `agents`, `outputStyles`, and `workflows` replace their default folder when the manifest sets them; `skills` is the one that adds. Listing only `./extra/status.md` turns off the scan of `commands/`, which is why the plugin still loads cleanly while three of its commands vanish. A missing `./` prefix (A) would fail validation loudly rather than quietly, so it cannot be this. No marketplace entry is needed — `--plugin-dir` loads a manifest-less plugin fine (C). Re-running the reload (D) is cargo cult; nothing about component scanning is cached across reloads.

questions.prompt: A hook needs to write a cache file so it does not re-download the same index on every session. The plugin updates weekly. Where should the file go?
options: Inside the plugin directory, referenced with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/.cache/index
In a directory referenced with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}, which is created on first reference and survives plugin updates
Next to the hook script in the plugin's scripts/ folder, next to the other bundled files
In the project's .claude/ folder, so every teammate's checkout gets the same cache
questions.explanation: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` points at the installed plugin directory, and that directory is replaced on every update — anything you wrote into it is destroyed the next time the plugin ships. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` exists for exactly this: installed dependencies, generated code, and caches that must outlive an update. Writing to the plugin directory (A) or to `scripts/` beside the hook (C) both work right up until the first update and then fail silently with a fresh, empty cache. The project's `.claude/` (D) is for files you commit on purpose, and a downloaded cache has no business being committed.

questions.prompt: You copy an installed plugin to a scratch folder and start a session with `claude --plugin-dir ./scratch-copy`. It loads. Its two skills are gone, its agent is there, and `/plugin` → Errors names a path it could not find. The original works fine. What did the copy do wrong?
options: The manifest lost its `name` field when copied, so components had nothing to namespace under
The `skills/` directory ended up inside `.claude-plugin/` instead of beside it, where nothing scans for components
A copied plugin loses its `version`, so Claude Code refuses to load skills at that version
The `.zip`-style copy broke path separators, so `skills/` was found but `SKILL.md` inside it was not
questions.explanation: Only `plugin.json` belongs inside `.claude-plugin/`; a `skills/` directory parked there is not scanned, so its skills silently do not load while every other component type in the same copy loads fine — which is exactly the asymmetry being reported. A missing `name` (A) would either fail validation or make the loader complain about the manifest itself, not leave agents working. `version` is metadata, not a gate (C). Broken separators (D) invent a failure mode that doesn't exist on any platform this runs on, and would not produce a single clean 'path not found' line.
